outcome: perceived risk of maternal health outcomes
negative impact on the couple's relationship
cohort: 264 nulliparous women at 36-40 weeks gestation and their partners
finding: Women who underwent cesarean delivery continued to perceive higher risks of certain health outcomes after delivery compared to vaginal delivery, despite a general decrease in perceived risks for most outcomes after both modes of delivery.
mod_finding: Women perceived higher risks of long-term perineal pain, pelvic organ prolapse, urinary/fecal incontinence, sexual dissatisfaction, and negative impact on the couple's relationship after VD than after CD.
